title: Homogeneous coordinates for continuous cochains with topological coefficients
statement:
Let $E$ be a topological field [def-weil-field], $J$ a topological group, and $V$ a topological $E$-vector space with a jointly continuous $E$-linear $J$-action. Let $B^n(J,V)$ consist of the jointly continuous functions $F:J^{n+1}\to V$ satisfying $F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_n)=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ for every $a\in J$, with pointwise $E$-vector space structure and differential
$$(\delta F)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^iF(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{n+1}).$$
Let $C^n(J,V)=C(J^n,V)$, $C^0(J,V)=V$, with differential
$$(df)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n),$$
including $(dv)(g)=gv-v$. These are ordinary complexes of abstract $E$-vector spaces, extended by zero in negative degrees. In the derived category $D(E\text{-Vect})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there is a natural isomorphism $Q(B^\bullet(J,V))\simeq Q(C^\bullet(J,V))$, represented by an actual $E$-linear cochain isomorphism $\Phi:B^\bullet(J,V)\to C^\bullet(J,V)$ with inverse $\Psi$, given by
$$(\Phi_nF)(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=F(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_n),$$
$$(\Psi_nf)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=x_0 f(x_0^{-1}x_1,x_1^{-1}x_2,\ldots,x_{n-1}^{-1}x_n).$$
Thus $\Phi_{n+1}\delta=d\Phi_n$ and $\Psi_{n+1}d=\delta\Psi_n$; in degree zero $\Phi_0F=F(1)$ and $\Psi_0v(x)=xv$. Both cochain isomorphisms commute with continuous equivariant $E$-linear coefficient maps and with restriction along continuous homomorphisms of topological groups (using the restricted action on $V$). No compactness, discreteness, completeness, or local compactness hypothesis is imposed.
